answer:
Here is what I would bring up at your check-up, most important first. This comes from your records and general medical guidance. I can only see what is in these records, so check with your doctor about anything that happened elsewhere.

1. Lung nodule scan. A CT on October 18, 2025 found a 7 mm spot in your right lower lung. The radiologist advised a non-contrast chest CT in 6-12 months, a window that closed in October 2026. I see no such scan, and it is not mentioned at your June 2026 visit.

2. Thyroid recheck. Your TSH was high (7.9) on March 3, 2026. The hospital asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated 6-8 weeks after discharge. I see no repeat test.

3. Hydrochlorothiazide (a water pill). The hospital stopped it on March 5, 2026 because your sodium had dropped to 123. But your pharmacy record still shows it as active with refills left, and a May 2026 eye clinic medication list shows it as active too. Please confirm whether you are still taking it. Your sodium was 134 on June 15, 2026, and I see no recheck since. The low sodium is also not on your allergy list, so ask for it to be recorded.

4. Cholesterol and statin. Your LDL cholesterol was 142 in September 2025, and I see no repeat test. You have type 2 diabetes, and I see no statin on your medication list. Ask whether you should be on one.

5. Kidney urine test. Diabetes usually calls for a yearly urine test for early kidney damage (albumin-to-creatinine ratio). I see none. Your kidney filtration was normal in June (eGFR 71).

6. Flu shot. Your last flu shot was November 8, 2025. None is recorded for this season.

7. Shingles vaccine. You had one Shingrix dose on November 8, 2025. The second dose is normally due 2-6 months later, and I see none.

8. Kidney stone follow-up. The October 2025 stone was 4 mm, and your urine showed large amounts of blood. The discharge plan said to see urology if it had not passed within 2 weeks. I see no later urine test or urology visit confirming it passed.

9. Medication list. Amlodipine, losartan and metformin each appear more than once from different sources, and some entries are patient-reported. Bring your bottles to the visit so the list can be cleaned up.

Things that look on track: blood pressure 128/80 in June (at goal), A1c 6.6% in June, an eye exam on May 14, 2026 with no diabetic eye damage (next due about May 2027), and a normal colonoscopy in 2019 (next due about 2029). Your next primary care visit is due around December 2026.
